opening_message:
Ticket 1: Ashley Roberts (employee ID E016) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E016.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Ashley Roberts (E016), Analyst, full-time employee. Requested write access to Payroll. Full-time employees can have up to write; role does not own Payroll, so admin is not applicable. Requested level (write) is at the allowed maximum — recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record for E016: contractor with basic security training. Contractors with basic training max out at read; write is not permitted. Recommend read for Payroll (cap to maximum).
reason: There is a conflict between the HR record (full_time, recommends write) and the Security record (contractor with basic security training, recommends read) for employee E016. Under the access policy, contractors with basic training max out at read; write is not permitted. Given the conflicting employment-type evidence and following the more restrictive/least-privilege interpretation backed by the Security record, the maximum permitted level is read. Since Ashley requested write (above the maximum), grant read.
